Clara is a research workbench on one machine, Alita. Ask a question from your phone or terminal. Everything happens inside that box.
Inside Alita, Clara writes code, trains the model, and inspects results. Data never leaves. Clara has no network access, so patient data stays local.
A relay sits in front of Clara and reads every request first. Requests naming a data path, subject id, cohort name or image file go to the local model. Data-free work goes to Cle, the model hub.
The work splits in two. Cle and the research agents reach the network and never see data. Clara sees data and never reaches the network. The relay is the wall.
The path is short. A question becomes a shortlist of methods. Each method becomes a job with countable acceptance criteria. The harness runs one job at a time until the check passes.
At the end you get a trained model, a comparison table and a QC page. One question in, one checked result out, all on Alita.
